findings.summary: Active-channel capacity validation can be bypassed by mixed membership rows
findings.details: The persisted mutation reads at most 101 sourceChannels for the organization before invoking the planner, but the table index ranges across every membershipStatus when only organizationKey is constrained. Organizations with non-active channel rows in that prefix can hide the 101st joined/active channel from buildBulkPolicyPlan, so a policy change can be accepted even though the launch envelope requires rejecting more than 100 active joined channels.

findings.summary: Policy lifecycle and replay safety truncate immutable history at 500 rows
findings.details: The real mutation derives the next routing epoch, delivery generation, active-policy match, and active-pointer deactivation from only the first 500 policy rows for an organization. Immutable rollback/change history is unbounded by the task contract, so after enough policy epochs the current active row can fall outside that prefix; a retry or rollback can then insert a duplicate epoch/generation and leave a stale active policy unpatched instead of deterministically moving one active pointer.

findings.summary: Denied privileged policy changes are not audited
findings.details: S04-T04 includes IAM-04, whose baseline requires privileged success and denial auditing. The mutation records slack.channelPolicyChanged only after a plan succeeds; signed-in users without an active admin/owner membership fail in loadPolicyActor before any denied audit event is written.
